records.summary: Advancing outward, the integrity of reality becomes increasingly compromised in Fragmentia. Here, what was once solid and tangible becomes inconsistent and fragmented, with realities splintering and drifting like fractured shards. outer exosphere Description: Fragmentia is a fractured expanse where reality itself breaks apart into shards, each a splintered remnant of different worlds or timelines. These fragmented pieces drift unpredictably, creating a chaotic environment that tests playersʼ agility, perception, and resilience.

records.proposedName: Hazardous Corners and “Soft Spots” in Reality
records.summary: - Spatial Anomalies: Certain areas feel “thin,” with walls or floors that may become permeable, revealing glimpses into other realities. Moving through these areas requires Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks (DC 15) to avoid falling through. - Memory Drift Zones: Specific areas cause memory distortion, where players may lose focus or experience short-term memory loss. Characters must make Wisdom saving throws (DC 14) each hour or lose awareness of their location or companions. ---

Mechanic: Objects and entities shift unpredictably in Deliquium. Anything held or recognized may change form unexpectedly. Roll for Form Change: Every 10 minutes, roll a d20. On a roll of 1-5, any held item or familiar object changes form (e.g., a sword becomes a vine, a path becomes a river). Reverting Objects: Objects revert to their original form within 1 hour of leaving Deliquium. Players can use Intelligence (Arcana) checks (DC 14) to briefly “hold” a chosen shape.

◦ To travel physically, the character must locate and interact with a lucid gateway or transitional point. ◦ Check: Require a DC 15 Athletics check (to physically step into the gateway) combined with a DC 14 Wisdom (Awareness) check to confirm the gatewayʼs authenticity. ◦ Effect: On success, the characterʼs body “shifts” into the Dreaming Realms, experiencing both the tangible hazards and the surreal effects described in each layer. •Risks & Limitations: ◦ Physical bodies in the Dreaming Realms are more vulnerable to hazards such as environmental psychic feedback (taking 1d4 psychic or physical damage on a failed Constitution check in Abyssus Somni). ◦ Exposure in physical mode intensifies encounters with lucid entities—beneficial or hostile—who can more directly interact with the traveler.

Long rests are extremely difficult, as the environment subtly resists extended periods of inactivity. Characters attempting long rests must succeed on Wisdom saving throws (DC 16) to avoid sleep disturbances or vivid nightmares.

Mechanic: Dream entities are sentient beings native to Visium who are aware of travelers. Characters may encounter them as guides, guardians, or wandering dreamers. Interaction: Negotiation or distraction requires Charisma-based checks (DC 13-15). Entities may assist, ignore, or attempt to interact meaningfully depending on the playerʼs actions and intentions. Risk: Repeated interactions increase the risk of these entities realizing players are outsiders, leading to potential hostility.

Distinct Laws of Reality: Each universe in the Sea of Realities has its own rules. Characters must make an Intelligence (Investigation) check (DC 13) upon entering a new reality to understand the core rules, such as gravity, time flow, or magical influence.

- Every hour, players must make an Intelligence saving throw (DC 15) to retain their memories. Failure results in temporary memory loss, causing characters to forget recent events, personal details, or even why they entered Uneksia. - Memory Loss Duration: Memory loss lasts until players leave Uneksia or pass a successful Intelligence save. Players may experience brief flashes of clarity where memories return in fragments. - Memory Triggers: Strong sensory cues (smells, colors, or sounds) may briefly restore forgotten memories. GMs can provide hints by describing familiar sensations or objects from charactersʼ pasts.

- Mechanic: Certain areas in Prenihila accelerate memory loss and Reality Bleed, causing characters to experience amnesia-like effects. - Memory Check: Characters must make Wisdom (Insight) checks (DC 16) every time they pass through these zones. Failure results in the loss of a specific memory or detail, making navigation and decision-making increasingly difficult. - Restoration Attempts: Recalling memories requires a successful Wisdom (Perception) check (DC 14) and may involve encountering a Memory Echo or relic that helps restore lost details.

- Memory Bleeding: Prolonged time in Uneksia increases the risk of losing personal memories. Players who fail three consecutive Intelligence saving throws experience more significant memory loss, including names, skills, or recent events. - Fog of Forgetting: Certain rooms or areas are “memory traps” where memories are siphoned away, requiring Wisdom (Perception) checks (DC 14) to avoid wandering into these zones unknowingly.

- Encounter: Shadowy entities seek out the memories of living beings. Players encountering them must make Wisdom saving throws (DC 15) to avoid the wraiths siphoning a minor memory (a recent event or specific detail). - Recovery Opportunity: If players successfully resist, they gain Advantage on their next Intelligence saving throw to retain their memories.

- Entities within Translimina sometimes feed on memories, briefly draining players of a specific recollection. When encountered, players must make Wisdom saves (DC 16) to avoid losing a personal memory or skill temporarily. - Dreamlike entities appear as flickering forms of people or places from playersʼ pasts, prompting nostalgia or anxiety. Interaction with these forms requires Wisdom (Perception) checks (DC 15) to avoid emotional distress. ---

- Each room or corridor may repeat indefinitely. Every 30 minutes, characters must make Intelligence (Investigation) checks (DC 14) to identify patterns and escape loops. Failure traps them in a loop for an additional 30 minutes.

- The ground and structures in Uneksia may shift from solid to ethereal without warning. Each hour, players must make Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks (DC 14) to navigate safely across unstable surfaces or risk falling or slipping. - Failure Consequence: On a failed check, players may stumble and find themselves briefly suspended between reality and dream, taking 1d4 psychic damage and losing track of their location until they regain their balance.

Mechanic: Visual cues are almost entirely absent, with the realm relying on auditory and tactile sensations. Players must adapt to this disorienting experience. Perception Penalty: All Perception checks rely on hearing and touch, with a -5 penalty due to the lack of sight.

Finally, at the multiverse's very fringe, Oblivion stands—a realm of unyielding void. It's the culmination of the journey, where all traces of existence and essence dissipate into absolute nothingness. (outer space) Description: The very edge of existence, where all essence dissipates into nothingness.

Mechanic: Prolonged exposure to Deliquium begins to dissolve playersʼ physical forms, blending them with the environment. Dissolution Check: Every hour, players must make a Constitution saving throw (DC 14). Failure causes mild disorientation and disadvantage on Strength-based checks as parts of their bodies start to “blur.” Restoration: Constitution saves can eventually stabilize characters, or they may need to exit Deliquium for the effects to fade completely.

- Visual Displacement: Characters occasionally perceive their surroundings as if they were shifted a few feet from their true position. Players must make Constitution saves (DC 14) to avoid vertigo, which imposes disadvantage on Dexterity checks. - Memory Fades: Prolonged exposure causes memories to fade in certain rooms. Every hour, players must make Wisdom saves (DC 15) or lose track of the last few minutes, making it challenging to recall recent actions or companions.

Mechanic: Fragmentia consists of floating shards of various worlds, each with different gravitational pulls, climates, and orientations. Navigation: Characters must make Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks (DC 15) every 30 minutes to move safely across these shards without slipping or falling into the void between them. Failure Consequence: On a failed check, a character may slip, requiring a Strength (Athletics) check (DC 13) to catch hold of a nearby shard or take 1d6 falling damage before finding another stable foothold.

- Drifting Objects: Items or fixtures may shift location when unobserved, creating subtle disorientation. Roll a d6 every 10 minutes; on a 1-2, any unobserved objects in the area move or disappear. - Unreliable Gravity and Slanting Floors: Certain rooms have tilted or fluctuating gravity, requiring Dexterity saving throws (DC 13) to avoid falls or slipping.

- Unpredictable Shifts: Parts of Uneksia suddenly “shift,” causing players to find themselves in different locations without moving. Roll a d4 every hour; on a 1-2, players are subtly repositioned within Uneksia, possibly separating them or returning them to areas they have already passed. - Floating Objects and Pathways: Objects and surfaces in Uneksia occasionally float or tilt, requiring Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks (DC 13) to avoid losing footing or letting go of items. ---

Mechanic: Occasionally, players encounter the sparse remnants of other realities: floating relics, translucent images, or faint sensory cues that evoke distant memories. Interacting with Remnants: Players may attempt Intelligence (Investigation) or Wisdom (Perception) checks (DC 14) to interact with these remnants, potentially gaining small items, bits of knowledge, or momentary boosts to skills. Remnant Effects: Retrieved items may have limited use outside Vacuousia, retaining ethereal properties that slowly fade after leaving.

Progressing further, the chaotic Convergence yields to the vast expanse of the Sea of Realities. In this expansive domain, infinite universes with distinct narratives, laws, and structures emerge, each a unique reflection of the multiverse's grand design. Think earths crust to troposphere Description: A boundless expanse of infinite, distinct realities, each with its unique laws, narratives, and structures.

Mechanic: Players experience powerful waves of sensation that may overwhelm them. Every hour, players must make a Constitution saving throw (DC 14). Effects of Failure: Failure results in the player becoming overwhelmed, suffering 1d4 psychic damage and disadvantage on all Perception and Insight checks due to sensory overload. Bonus: Successfully withstanding the sensory overload grants temporary Advantage on Charisma (Persuasion or Deception) checks, as the player gains insight into emotions.

- Lurking Figures: Unidentifiable shadows follow or observe the players. Characters sensing these presences must make Charisma (Intimidation) or Wisdom (Perception) checks (DC 14) to maintain composure or risk taking 1d4 psychic damage from anxiety. - Echoes of Self: Players occasionally encounter distorted reflections of themselves, which seem to mimic their actions imperfectly. These reflections do not interact but may vanish when approached.

- Characters occasionally encounter shadowed figures mirroring their movements. These figures may vanish upon approach but leave behind hints in the form of written notes or whispered warnings. - In some cases, characters may have to face a shadowed version of themselves in a test of will. Defeating these reflections requires Wisdom saving throws (DC 16) to resist psychic damage and regain control.

Mechanic: The environment shifts into maze-like structures, with rooms, corridors, and stairways that change as players move through them. Navigation: To avoid becoming lost or separated, characters must make Intelligence (Investigation) checks (DC 15) every hour. Effects of Failure: A failed check disorients players, possibly separating them from the group or returning them to previously traversed areas.
Short rests are possible in stable rooms but carry the risk of reality shifting. Roll a d20; on a 5 or lower, players awaken to find their surroundings altered.

Mechanic: Objects and characters may randomly transform based on dream symbolism. Every hour, players must make a Wisdom saving throw (DC 13) to maintain their perception of reality. Effects of Failure: Characters risk taking on dream-like aspects (e.g., gaining wings, turning parts of their body into abstract shapes). These changes last 1d4 hours or until players succeed on another

- Mechanic: Massive, anchored forms of the first gods float near the edge of Prenihila, shrouded in dense fog and silence. Their presence, while dormant, resonates powerfully, subtly influencing the environment. - Resonance Effect: Characters within 100 feet of a slumbering god gain a +1 bonus to Wisdom saving throws, as the godʼs dormant power briefly reinforces their sense of self. - Echo of Divinity: Players who approach within 50 feet can attempt a Charisma (Persuasion or Religion) check (DC 18) to awaken a faint echo of the godʼs consciousness, receiving a one-time insight or boon. - Risks of Interaction: Failed checks may instead awaken a protective aspect of the godʼs essence, causing characters to experience temporary stat penalties (such as -1 to Charisma or Wisdom for 1 hour) as they feel overwhelmed by the godʼs presence. ---

Mechanic: Lucid gateways exist as shimmering doorways, mirrors, or archways, linking Visium to deeper layers of the Dreaming Realms. Finding Gateways: Players can discover these portals with a Wisdom (Insight) check (DC 14). Once found, they may choose to pass through, taking them to different dream layers or allowing them to “descend” to Somnara. Unstable Travel: Once a gateway is used, it may close behind them, preventing easy return. Every hour, thereʼs a 25% chance that previously used portals disappear or relocate. Below is a proposed supplement to your Dreaming Realms rules that explicitly distinguishes between two modes of travel: one for the dream state (conscious projection) and one for physically entering the realms. This way, you can maintain the “dreamlike” mechanics already in place while also incorporating rules for full-body, multiversal travel.

Venturing farther, one encounters the vast voids of Vacuousia. Echoes of realities long past are sparse and distant, leaving behind an almost desolate expanse of emptiness, where the remnants of existence are but whispers. (outer magnetosphere) Description: Vacuousia is a nearly featureless, desolate expanse filled only with the echoes of realities long past. This realmʼs endless emptiness drains players physically and mentally, leaving only faint traces of existence that serve as fragmented reminders of what once was.

- Mechanic: Fading echoes of reality occasionally appear as fragile, floating remnants of past worlds —shattered fragments that offer both intrigue and risk. - Interaction Checks: Characters may make Intelligence (Arcana) or Wisdom (Insight) checks (DC 15) to interact with these remnants, which can grant insights or brief memories of previous worlds. - Risks of Interaction: On a failed check, characters experience a “void pull,” temporarily losing a memory or skill as if it were siphoned away. ---

•Some buildings are unstable, with sections that collapse without warning. A failed Dexterity saving throw (DC 13) results in 2d6 bludgeoning damage and restrained movement until freed. 2.Diseased Water: •Pools of stagnant water are breeding grounds for disease. Characters stepping into or drinking from these sources must make a Constitution saving throw (DC 14) to avoid infection, which causes 1 point of Constitution damage each day until cured. 3.Hidden Tripwires: •Thieves and gangs often lay traps in abandoned alleys. A Wisdom (Perception) check (DC 15) detects them; failure triggers the trap, causing 2d6 piercing damage or immobilizing the character with a net. 4.Gang Ambush Points: •Gangs mark territory with symbols only locals recognize. Players entering these areas risk ambush. Perception checks (DC 12) can detect hidden gang members preparing an attack.

•General Goods Stalls: Offer essentials like rations, clothing, and common tools. •Artisan Stalls: Specialize in crafted items such as jewelry, pottery, and armor. •Alchemy and Potion Vendors: Sell healing potions, poisons, and rare herbs. •Exotic Goods Stalls: Offer rare and foreign items, though some may be illegal or cursed. •Food Stalls: Sell street food and delicacies, which can restore HP or provide temporary buffs. 2.Crowd Conditions: •Busy Hours: At peak times, the marketplace becomes difficult terrain. Players must make Dexterity (Acrobatics) checks (DC 12) to avoid being pushed or jostled by the crowd. •Quiet Hours: During off-peak times, vendors are more eager to make sales, granting advantage on Persuasion checks for bargains. 3.Weather Conditions: •Sunny Days: Vendors are lively and eager to sell, creating a festive atmosphere. •Rainy Days: Some stalls close, limiting options, but buyers may find discounts from vendors desperate to sell before leaving. •Market Festivals: On special market days, rare items or events occur, but prices may rise due to increased demand.

Characters passing through public spaces may encounter bards or activists. These encounters can offer entertainment, clues, or hidden motives. 2.Protests or Riots: Characters caught in civil unrest must make Dexterity saving throws (DC 15) to avoid injury or getting swept up in the chaos. Guards may impose curfews or arrest individuals caught in restricted areas. 3.Marketplace Shenanigans: •Merchant Scam: An NPC offers a magical item for an outrageous price. A Wisdom (Insight) check (DC 14) reveals the scam. •Auction War: Players can bid against wealthy NPCs for rare items. Success requires a contested Charisma (Deception) or Intelligence (Economics) roll. 4.Organized Crime: •Gang Ambush: Roll for initiative! Criminals may attempt to rob or recruit the players. •Assassination Contract: A character may unknowingly become a target. The party must either protect them or confront the assassins.

•Slow: 10 miles per day •Normal: 15 miles per day •Fast: 20 miles per day (increased exhaustion risk for animals and people) 2.Setting up Camp: •Setting up or breaking down the camp takes 2 hours for a small group, or 4 hours for a large caravan. During setup, characters must make Wisdom (Survival) checks (DC 12) to find secure locations for tents and supply wagons.
•Entering the wrong alley triggers a gang ambush. Players must fight or negotiate their way out to avoid losing credits or gear.
